messages:
maya: Seeing a weird sawtooth in tokens/sec on prod after the 2026-03-15 merge. Route: /v1/generate on model rdx-3b-quant. Tokens/s oscillates ~12k -> ~6k every ~40-60s. No obvious OOMs. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/RED123 (looks like bursts then drains)
jonathan: Hmm. Could be batcher oscillation or a kernel selection thrash. Any scheduler traces or batch size distribution?
maya: I grabbed a handful of traces from the continuous-batcher service. Queueing delay spikes line up with kernel_selector log churn. Example from one host:
```
[2026-03-15T18:21:03Z] kernel_selector: chosen kernel=quant_fast batch=6 memcopy=10us
[2026-03-15T18:21:45Z] kernel_selector: fallback kernel=fp32_safe batch=3 memcopy=1200us
[2026-03-15T18:22:20Z] kernel_selector: chosen kernel=quant_fast batch=6 memcopy=9us
[2026-03-15T18:23:05Z] kernel_selector: fallback kernel=fp32_safe batch=2 memcopy=1300us
```
maya: When it falls back to fp32_safe throughput tanks and queueing latency spikes for ~30-45s until it recovers.
sasha: That log pattern matches the prefetch/policy tweak from PR #842 — I changed adaptive prefetch to be more aggressive (lookahead=2 -> 4) to try and boost batching. It might be causing probe batches that trigger small-batch fp32 fallback.
jonathan: If PR 842 is the suspect, can we reproduce by flipping lookahead back to 2 in a canary? Also need KV cache hitrate and prefix cache stats — fallback might be triggered by low KV contiguity.
maya: Quick local canary: forcing lookahead=2 on one pool removed the sawtooth on that pool (tokens/sec stable). KV stats on the affected host:
```
kv_cache.hits: 72.1%
kv_cache.misses: 27.9%
kvcache.evictions_per_min: 1.2
```
maya: Hitrate is lower than other pools (normally ~86-89%). Not huge but could interact with small-batch probes.
perf-bot: CI perf suite reported regressions in nightly runs after merge 4b9c7d: latency p95 +18% on x86, +22% on ampere. Builds: 2026-03-15-4b9c7d. Full report: https://ci.internal/run/5678
jonathan: Let's get a pprof of the worst host while it's in the low-throughput interval. Run `pprof -text srv:9090 profile` and look for memcpy/memmove hotspots and scheduler wait durations.
maya: Pprof snippet from low interval:
```
(pprof) top
  45.8%  kernel_switch memcpy
  23.4%  batch_scheduler wait_for_batch
  12.1%  kernel_selector evaluate_cost
```
maya: memcpy dominates when we fall back — looks like kernel path changes cause extra memory copies (cpu->gpu layout) for fp32_safe.
eric: If memcpy is causing the long tail we should either optimize the fallback path or avoid falling back by biasing selection toward quant kernels unless a hard failure. Can we add a short-term guard that requires two consecutive evaluation signals before switching kernel?
sasha: I can draft a conservative fix to gate fallback with a 2x confirmation window. That should stop oscillation while we analyze deeper kernel heuristics.
jonathan: Also add metrics: `kernel_selector.switch_count`, `kernel_selector.last_switch_age`, and a histogram of `batch_size_on_switch`. Those would have made this obvious earlier.
maya: I'm opening an issue and a bisect task now. Tentative suspect: PR #842 change to lookahead + kernel heuristic interplay. If folks agree I can push a revert patch to unblock rollout.
sasha: I support the revert if canary holds. I can also push the confirmation-gate patch to the same branch for fast test.
perf-bot: Marking CI regressions as P1 for this release. See perf-alert #9012.
deploy-bot: Rollout hold scheduled for release 2026-03-16T02:00Z pending manual action. If revert branch merges, set override flag.
maya: I'll open the bisect issue with the candidate commit list and start a controlled canary on two hosts with lookahead=2 and confirm gate enabled. Will post results in thread.
eric: Thanks — please also add a short perf test that repros the sawtooth using a synthetic workload (prefix variance + KV miss pattern) so CI can catch it next time.
maya: On it. Will attach synthetic load script and perf profile once I finish.
deploy-bot: rollback scheduled at 1910009000 (planned) — react with :thumbsup: if this is good to proceed.
